reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

surfaces.part: side body with windows, doors and green stripe

answer.evidence: The bus is drawn side-on, facing west. Rows 1-23 form a wide, light roof band with roof hatches. It ends in a front-edge line at row 24 (L=162), followed by darker eave shadow at rows 25-26 (L=130, then 81). Below that is a vertical south face from rows 27 to 54 with windows, doors, a green stripe and a dark underside. Two wheels hang below it, which is normal. The roof is a real top surface of 20+ rows over a front face of 28 rows. The object is a vehicle, so the 'box' kind only loosely fits.

styleAnswer.evidence: The bus is a big prop, and the references are small props of the same kind. Its measured 88% near-neutral dark edge pixels, plus the visible dark grey-black contour around the body, wheels and windows, give the uniform sticker outline. The references use tinted outlines: the hedge is at 0%, the cheese stall at 1% and the well at 33%. The white roof and the lower body are broad, almost flat panels with only a light dither and a few steps, about 3-4 per material against the 5-6 on the stall and well. Near-flat coverage is 18%, above the 0% of the hedge and well and the 13% of the stall. Visible tones per tile are 10, close to the hedge's 9 but well under the well's 20 and the stall's 17. The wheels, windows and green stripe carry some detail, but the roof and side panels lack the grain, per-element highlights and material-toned edges of the references. Overall it looks flatter and more sticker-like than the references.

surfaces.part: bus side body with windows, doors and green stripe

answer.evidence: The bus is drawn in side profile facing west. A large pale roof plane covers rows 1-23 and carries roof hatches. It ends in a front-edge line at row 24, followed by darker eave shadow at rows 25-26 and a green trim line at row 27. Below it is a south face of about 28 rows (rows 27-54) with windows, doors and a green stripe. Wheels extend to row 62. The roof plane is far more than a rim, so the body shows both a top surface and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The bus is a large piece, so the measured facts apply. It has 10 visible tones per tile, roughly level with the hedge (9) but well below the stall (17) and well (20). Its dark edge pixels are 88% near-neutral, which fits a black-grey sticker outline. The references that carry material-tinted outlines (stall 1%, hedge 0%) are quite different. The white roof and body are very large, almost flat panels with only light dither and a thin shadow edge, so they have roughly 2-3 steps. They lack the 5-6 step ramps and per-element texture of the Beodeul pieces. The window frames, doors and wheels are shaded decently, but the bulk of the piece is a flat fill with a neutral outline. Near-flat coverage is 18%, higher than every reference (0-13%). This falls short of the Beodeul standard.

surfaces.part: body side with windows, doors and green stripe

answer.evidence: A large pale band at rows 2-23 reads as a roof plane. Rooftop units with light tops and darker fronts sit on it, and it ends in a light edge line at row 24 followed by darker shadow at rows 25-26 and a green trim line at row 27. Below it the side face runs from row 27 to about row 54, with doors, windows and wheels. The bus is a vehicle in side view rather than a box, so the kind match is doubtful. The roof band is tall and might also be a white upper body panel, which makes this reading uncertain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The bus is a large, mostly white body with a dark navy-grey outline, and 88% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline reads as a uniform dark sticker line rather than the dark tone of each material. The white roof and body show only about 3 steps (white, light grey, grey), with a little dither at the roof edge. The windows, doors and wheels are clean but lightly shaded, and the body panels are large smooth areas. The measured 10 visible tones per tile is comparable to the hedge (9) but well below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 18%, higher than every reference (0-13%), which confirms the large flat panels. The piece is cleanly drawn and has some dither and window detail, but it is shallower than the references in ramp depth and outline craft.

surfaces.part: side wall with windows, doors and green stripe

answer.evidence: Rows 2-23 form a large near-white roof plane with three raised vent hatches. It ends in a light edge line at row 24, followed by darker eave shadow at rows 25-26 and a dark green trim line at row 27. Below it, rows 28-53 show the south side face with windows, two doors, a green stripe and a lower skirt, which makes a front face of about 26 rows. The wheels extend down to row 62. The tail light is at the right end, so the bus faces west. The side face is the normal south face, not a receding side.

styleAnswer.evidence: The bus is a large prop, and its outline and body construction look sticker-like next to the references. The dark edge pixels are 88% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line around the body, wheels and windows. That is unlike the tinted outlines of the hedge (0%) and cheese stall (1%). The white roof and body are large, nearly flat areas with only a faint dither and one or two light-grey steps, so the main material ramp has about 3 steps against the references' 5-6. The window and door panels are flat dark blocks. Visible tones per tile are 10, close to the hedge (9) but well under the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 18%, above the 0-13% of the references. The candidate does have some detail in the windows, the green stripe and the wheels, so texture is partial. The neutral outline, shallow body shading and flat fills still put it below the Beodeul bar.
